name: Furnace of the First Breach
title: What the mountain kept
summary: An abandoned furnace can replace a ruined harbour’s winter anchors. Its last operator and the animal nesting below it both intend to keep the heat.
spatialIdentity: A cylindrical excavation establishes three legible strata: dry ore galleries, a furnace ring and cooling trenches. A broken hanging elevator joins them only when the counterweight crosses an exposed shaft. Heat lanes remain visible through smoke and mineral colour changes.
inhabitants: Blind trench grazers consume warm mineral films.
Displaced foundry workers shelter in an upper counting room.
Vorrak feeds below the furnace ring; Ithraden occupies its shutter controls.
discoveries: A production ledger records anchors recast as siege collars.
The missing elevator counterweight is a nursery shelf, not discarded stone.
A cold bypass can restart the furnace at reduced output without draining the nesting trenches.
history: The first breach was industrial: workers cut a cooling bore into a living fault and mistook the pressure release for an inexhaustible source. Subsequent military contracts deepened the bore. The evacuation left a furnace that still consumes its own foundations; recent Void Ascendant occupation has accelerated the damage.
traversal: Read soot shadows to time furnace shutters, transfer the elevator counterweight and descend by maintenance chains. The reduced-output bypass supports a slower, safer extraction; full output produces more anchors but destroys the lower nursery and makes Vorrak permanently hostile.

story.role: A contract for winter anchors sends the pair into a still-burning foundry. They discover that the same alloy is supplying a mountain gun, and their choice of furnace output determines whether they can follow that shipment in time.

name: The Pelagic Cathedral
title: Where the current enters
summary: A drowned garrison has dammed the only warm current feeding an immense filter reef. Divers seeking a winter sea route must choose which military works to dismantle before the reef collapses.
spatialIdentity: Ancient black stairs run through younger living limestone ribs. Traversal alternates between air pockets, submerged bridges and a cobalt central gulf; pressure doors create explicit safe transitions. The giant shell valve is a living filter, not a treasure chest.
inhabitants: Filter colonies and shoals occupy the warm inlet.
Tide Witness divers maintain air bells in three side vaults.
Serath patrols the feeding gulf; Morvane guards the occupation standard.
discoveries: Diver scratches mark currents that contradict the surviving military chart.
A sealed granary contains a dated account of the garrison’s deliberate inundation.
The reef valve can be opened by clearing sediment while its feeding cilia are relaxed.
history: A coastal fort was abandoned to a rising sea; centuries of filter growth transformed its parade vault into a reef. A later occupying force anchored an enchanted standard across the inlet and drowned when its commanders refused evacuation. Residual Shadow corruption binds Morvane to that obstruction, not to a newly opened connection with Malachar.
traversal: Move between bounded breath stations, anchor before pressure changes and follow suspended silt to identify current direction. The descent remains accessible after combat. Opening the inlet increases visibility and food transport while making the return swim faster and more dangerous.

story.role: The divers reopen a starved reef inlet and recover evidence of a refused evacuation. Their new route reaches a mountain trade station whose seed stock may save the coastal harvest.

mythology.publicStory: Divers call the reef a cathedral built by the sea for people who never received burial.
mythology.counterStory: Old garrison songs insist the fort was given to the water by a victorious commander.
mythology.observableEvidence: The inundation ledger records a refused evacuation, and the filter reef is younger than the stairs.
mythology.unresolved: The first singer of the drowned dedication is unknown; the reef’s biological history does not decide that authorship.

name: Sepulchre of the Hollow Choir
title: The dead were not silent
summary: A burial avenue is being converted into a long-range weapon. Every chamber gives the invaders another resonator, and every occupied chamber contains witnesses whose evidence must survive the assault.
spatialIdentity: Immense horizontal ceramic bells form a sequence of traversable burial chambers. Cedar braces, low side tunnels and textile baffles create distinct acoustic routes. A straight avenue promises speed but exposes the traveller to the entire bell line.
inhabitants: Ceramic-boring beetles shelter in glaze cracks.
Two living custodians have barricaded the unamplified ossuary annex.
The Marrow Regent nests in the fourth bell; Vaust operates the far tuning frame.
discoveries: Different firing marks date several waves of burial migration.
Vaust’s notes show which resonator tissues he harvested from the Regent.
The custodians kept ordinary letters, recipes and debts alongside prestigious tomb records.
history: The avenue began as a refuge for migrants forbidden burial within the neighbouring city. Its bells were intended to carry names across the escarpment. A Void Ascendant cell seized the far chambers and converted remembrance into range-finding; the original name plates now survive only in the quieter annex.
traversal: Listen to brace knocks and watch dust lift before crossing exposed intervals. Move felt baffles to shorten dangerous acoustic paths; their weight leaves hands occupied. Breaking a bell creates a shortcut but permanently destroys its inscriptions, while releasing braces lowers it intact and blocks the avenue.

story.role: An occupied burial avenue hides a siege calibration method. Saving the quieter annex yields supply references to a vanished road survey, while destroying it leaves a faster but less provable trail.

mythology.counterStory: The city’s former magistrates dismissed the avenue as a burial ground without legitimate witnesses.

mythology.unresolved: A few names occur in several incompatible family accounts. Their relationships remain an archival question.

name: The Thorn Meridian
title: A border the forest never accepted
summary: An old survey cut divides a canopy expedition from its supplies. A rival hunter has claimed the only safe aqueduct, while a breeding arthropod uses its piers as a territorial drum.
spatialIdentity: A straight survey scar intersects a sinuous stone aqueduct suspended over ravines. The white watch platform remains visible through changing canopy layers. Deliberate long sightlines alternate with close roots, so hunter and prey gain different advantages.
inhabitants: Bark skimmers graze the survey stones.
Independent canopy surveyors maintain two rope camps.
Orryx controls the aqueduct joints; Serevra commands the white platform.
discoveries: Old boundary nails are embedded inside trees younger than the survey itself.
A molting shelf reveals Orryx’s seasonal vulnerability and a clutch beyond it.
Serevra’s claim covers a rescue route her expedition rebuilt, not ownership of the forest.
history: An early road authority cleared a ruler-straight passage and abandoned it when the ravine bridges failed. The surviving aqueduct became a migration corridor. Recent mineral surveys reopened the scar, concentrating traffic and arthropod territorial responses in the same narrow place.
traversal: Traverse rope routes with wind direction in mind; an unweighted line carries less noise than stone. Cutters shorten the route but expose the party to Serevra’s range. Reopen the old water channel to mask footfalls and let an escort pass without destroying the nesting piers.

story.role: A disputed crossing forces the surveyors to face an equally competent rival. Evidence of altered mineral growth beyond the frontier makes Serevra a necessary independent witness rather than a defeated obstacle.

mythology.counterStory: Canopy crews say the line survives only because generations of workers keep apologising with repairs.
mythology.observableEvidence: Boundary nails occur inside later tree growth; the restored water channel, not an oath, makes the crossing quiet.
mythology.unresolved: No surviving map establishes the first agreement between the road authority and the canopy settlements.

name: Bastion of Fallen Suns
title: The day became artillery
summary: A fortress once used the sun to deny entire valleys passage. Its last active engine now obstructs an evacuation, and an occupying captain wants to restore the artillery network.
spatialIdentity: Three broken concave mirrors dominate a steep citadel. Exposed ammunition lifts and military ramps make range and cover readable. Moving mirror shadows announce future firing lanes before the beam arrives; there is no pervasive glow to conceal them.
inhabitants: High-altitude scavengers nest behind cold mirror facets.
An evacuation column waits in an underground cistern.
The Sundered Engine patrols the firing ring; Rhaum controls the supply ramp.
discoveries: Supply tablets reveal the fortress could never sustain a full winter siege.
The Engine follows a perimeter map older than the present mountain road.
A manual defocus assembly survives behind the largest intact mirror.
history: The citadel’s apparent invincibility depended on imported food, clear skies and precise mirror crews. A storm destroyed two arrays during its last war. The remaining Engine continued an obsolete road-denial order. Rhaum’s recent occupation is an attempt to connect that old weapon to a new harbour campaign.
traversal: Cross firing lanes in moving shadow, counterbalance ammunition lifts and rotate abandoned observation shutters to create cover. Defocusing the surviving array preserves an observatory and removes its siege capability; smashing it is faster but showers the evacuation route with fragments.

story.role: The mountain road is blocked by obsolete artillery and a captain trying to claim it. Saving a stranded evacuation column costs the pair their best transport window but yields the blockade’s launch schedule.

mythology.counterStory: Valley households remembered them as borrowed daylight that could be taken back by weather.
mythology.observableEvidence: Supply tablets and storm damage show the weapon’s dependence on food, clear sky and human calibration.
mythology.unresolved: The original dedication may have been propaganda, sincere ritual or both; the machinery does not answer belief.

name: The Lacuna Stair
title: One chamber, an impossible return
summary: Surveyors disappear inside a stair that returns along its own ceiling. Their possessions emerge in the rain outside, rearranged by a rule that a patient observer can learn.
spatialIdentity: The spatial anomaly is confined to one black-stone chamber. A stair descends from the ordinary entrance and returns across the ceiling; marked landings form a small stable graph rather than unlimited random geometry. The mountain doorway remains an external reference.
inhabitants: Ordinary cave insects gather at the doorway and avoid the ceiling return.
A surviving surveyor maintains a chalk inventory at the third landing.
The Unfaced Pilgrim crosses marked steps; Ultharen changes the connections between them.
discoveries: Fresh chalk appears only on physically visited landings.
Every missing surveyor’s cord terminates at the same blocked junction.
An old tool cache predates the present stair configuration without explaining its maker.
history: Road crews uncovered the chamber while seeking a winter tunnel. Three incompatible survey diagrams describe locally repeatable observations. This proposal leaves the chamber’s maker and ultimate cause unresolved; its behaviours are experimental rules bounded to the site, not a revision of Arcanea’s cosmology.
traversal: Use a physical tether and numbered landing tokens to maintain orientation. Observe one complete reconfiguration before moving heavy loads. An external rope anchor establishes the escape route; falling returns the traveller to the last landing with lost time and damaged equipment, never an unexplained instant death.

story.role: The missing surveyors are trapped in a bounded impossible chamber. Their recovery provides an alternate exterior road plan; Jolant refuses to invent an origin story to make the report seem complete.

name: The Winter Reliquary
title: What survives the thaw
summary: A glacier has exposed a monastery’s seed vault just as its ice foundation starts to move. Two expeditions disagree over custody; a mountain predator has already claimed the warm evacuation channel.
spatialIdentity: Dark timber ribs hold a quarried ice interior above a thaw stream. Trapped air bands expose stresses in the floor; daylight from the far crevasse establishes direction. Weight, temperature and sound change which crossings remain usable.
inhabitants: Cold-water invertebrates feed below the thaw grates.
Two expedition crews occupy opposite ends of the nave.
Hroven shelters over the warm channel; Kethrane holds the seed-vault bridge.
discoveries: Wax-sealed seed jars record failed harvests as carefully as successful ones.
Iron restraint fragments document an abandoned attempt to use bears as glacier haulers.
The vault’s viable stock must warm gradually; immediate transport would ruin it.
history: The monastery stored mountain crops through a run of severe winters, then emptied when the trade route moved. Its builders used the glacier as a cold store without anticipating the present thaw. Kethrane’s expedition reached the seeds first and has already lost people establishing a controlled warming route.
traversal: Read ice whitening, spread weight over timber mats and divert thaw water without flooding the seed antechamber. Safe extraction takes time and cooperation; a fast retreat preserves lives but forfeits part of the viable stock. The central route remains traversable after Hroven is redirected.

story.role: Two expeditions must agree on custody while the seed vault thaws around them. Brigid’s rivalry with Kethrane becomes a workable alliance only when both crews accept visible losses and shared transport obligations.

mythology.counterStory: A later sponsor’s charter treated each jar as the founder’s property held through winter.
mythology.observableEvidence: Viability tests and warming records establish what can still grow; custody remains a human agreement.
mythology.unresolved: The founder’s intended ownership terms survive in conflicting copies and are not settled by the predator encounter.

name: The Verdant Crucible
title: A forest growing through its ore
summary: A mineral forest has become valuable enough to destroy. Its immense root organism maintains the crater’s water table, while a parasite and a hurried extraction crew destabilise the same terraces.
spatialIdentity: Terraced botanical laboratories surround a meteor crater. Living jade seams join root trunks, breathing sinkholes and a low stone causeway. Warm light penetrates translucent mineral growth without turning the forest into uniform neon.
inhabitants: Sap drinkers shelter in cool root channels.
A Meridian Survey extraction crew occupies a surviving laboratory.
The Verdigris Monarch supports the wet terraces; Khaross strips their conducting tissues.
discoveries: Early experiment notes distinguish native growth from introduced specimens.
Parasite casings show that small colonies prune obstructed channels.
A dry terrace offers a lower-yield seam that can be worked without cutting the root network.
history: A fallen mineral body altered the crater’s soils. Researchers cultivated its unusual growth, abandoned the site after a sinkhole collapse and left their instruments to be swallowed by roots. The present Monarch is a proposed local mutation, not an incarnation of a divine identity; accelerated extraction has turned ordinary parasitism into a system-wide outbreak.
traversal: Test stone causeways before committing weight, follow root pulsation to predict sinkholes and use insulated wedges to separate dead mineral from living tissue. Venting flooded laboratories changes both parasite routes and root access. The high-yield seam requires ecological destruction; the slower dry seam sustains a returnable expedition site.

story.role: A living mineral seam promises the expedition’s fortune until extraction accelerates a parasite outbreak. Fenwick must sign a lower-yield contract before knowing whether it will save his company.

mythology.counterStory: Miners tell the reverse tale: a forest slowly turning itself into a treasure house.
mythology.observableEvidence: Root channels carry water; small parasite colonies and destructive outbreaks have different effects.

name: Court of the Unbroken Light
title: Victory has a witness
summary: A roofless court offers a lawful contest for the right to reopen an ancient mountain passage. Its duelist honours exact terms; its sentinel executes older instructions whose consequences neither challenger nor judge can ignore.
spatialIdentity: Broad ivory stairs feed an almost empty central duel floor between clear quartz fins. Mountains and storm establish scale without obscuring silhouettes. Every refracted attack has a visible source, path and terminating surface.
inhabitants: Cliff swifts nest below the warm court floor.
Passage petitioners wait outside the measured boundary.
Avarra presides over the contest; the Prism Warden executes its surviving optical protocol.
discoveries: Successive versions of the trial charter disagree over the treatment of a surrendering entrant.
Footwear marks show previous victors sometimes returned as petitioners.
A bypass passage exists, but opening it would abandon the court’s protection against winter rockfall.
history: The court was built where rival valleys needed a passage neither would concede to the other. Its Celestial presider and Forged apparatus are new proposed identities, not Gate guardians. Later revisions made the contest less lethal without updating every mechanical condition; that discrepancy is a specific engineering and legal conflict, not universal corruption.
traversal: Observe a demonstration before entering, rotate spectator shutters to learn refraction and state the chosen victory condition. The duel can be won through boundary control and clean touches. Entering the sentinel’s maintenance lane during active judgement pauses scoring but exposes the entrant to its original defensive programme.

story.role: The mountain court can open the final route, but its old apparatus contradicts the terms of a fair trial. Brigid wins a passage and accepts a public maintenance duty, making the compact more durable than her own reputation.

mythology.counterStory: Petitioners also tell a less flattering story about exhausted armies that could no longer afford the pass.
mythology.observableEvidence: The charter revisions and optical apparatus are recoverable physical records.
mythology.unresolved: The relative weight of conviction and military exhaustion in the founding settlement remains a historian’s dispute.

name: The Blackwake Arsenal
title: The harbour has teeth
summary: An occupied drydock is building a blockade fleet over the feeding ground of a hull-breaking predator. The captives constructing the ships know where the admiral’s timetable can be broken.
spatialIdentity: Cliffside drydocks contain rain-slick gantries, suspended keels and chain capstans above tidal arches. Sea gates establish clear changes in water height. Each upper route has an observable lower consequence when a load is released.
inhabitants: Scavenger fish follow vibration beneath the keels.
Pressed shipwrights keep a concealed night roster.
Draeven commands the launch deck; the Keelbreaker feeds beneath it.
discoveries: The blockade depends on one week of favourable tides.
A shipwright’s repair marks identify chains deliberately made to fail under launch load.
The Keelbreaker attacks resonant hollow hulls and ignores quiet stone caissons.
history: The arsenal began as a communal storm refuge and became a fleet works when a new inland road connected its timber supply. Draeven seized it to launch a Void Ascendant blockade. His heavy pile-driving displaced the harbour predator; he now uses feeding alarms to punish escape attempts, making cruelty a tactical choice with an identifiable mechanism.
traversal: Read capstan gearing, coordinate tide windows and cross under suspended loads only after pinning their brakes. A controlled premature launch blocks the admiral’s fleet without sinking the workers’ evacuation boats. Release the predator into the open tide by removing the vibration source rather than herding it through inhabited docks.

story.role: The shipwrights sabotage their own launch work while Tamsin turns recovered components into a controlled premature launch. Liberation succeeds only if the harbour predator is given a quiet exit and the workers keep command of the rebuilt arsenal.

name: The Meridian of Ash
title: An observation worth a war
summary: An eclipse will reveal a buried lens well and the location of a viable desert water route. A scholar intends to monopolise the observation; a migrating mollusc is moving the ground beneath his instruments.
spatialIdentity: Salt-mesa chambers sit below enormous crescent instruments and knife-edge causeways. The eclipse changes illumination in predictable stages. Lens wells make vertical travel purposeful; exposed rings serve as both sighting geometry and shifting obstacles.
inhabitants: Nocturnal salt grazers emerge during the eclipse shadow.
Caravan water assessors wait below the mesa.
The Ashen Astronomer occupies the sighting ring; Veyrath follows buried brine beneath it.
discoveries: Several failed observations record bad weather rather than cosmic judgement.
Veyrath’s shell scars preserve the spacing of former desert watercourses.
The water route can be independently measured from two lower stations at reduced precision.
history: The observatory was founded to measure seasonal water beneath an advancing desert. Later scholars added a ceremonial reading of its instruments, but its material purpose survives in the notebooks. The Astronomer’s coercive monopoly is explicitly experimental independent mortal wrongdoing; neither the eclipse nor the mollusc is a source of cosmic evil.
traversal: Transport sighting components across low-wind intervals, clear buried marks and establish two lower observation stations before totality. Veyrath’s passage uncovers a lens well while closing the direct route. Missing the central observation changes confidence and expedition cost; it does not end the world.

story.role: The desert observation can validate the new route, but a scholar seeks exclusive control of the result. Corvin and Fenwick establish independent measurements during a colossal migration and publish the water map, earning a different business through trustworthy passage services.

name: The Wound Beneath the Stars
title: The frontier is not the prison
summary: A siege working on Shadowfen’s exterior is destroying the only bridge used by frontier evacuees. Its duelist is buying time to complete a local interdiction; the operation neither enters nor opens Malachar’s prison.
spatialIdentity: A root-lined ravine divides two ordinary frontier roads above black water. The severed causeway, six basalt anchor weights and unreachable opposite fissure establish the encounter’s limited geography. The canonical prison and the Source Gate remain offscreen and outside all traversal.
inhabitants: Root-burrowing scavengers occupy the higher dry banks.
A frontier convoy shelters behind the outer road embankment.
The Sable Testament controls six causeway anchors; Mordren protects their working lines.
discoveries: Anchor diagrams identify a bridge-destruction programme rather than a prison-opening ritual.
Supply records connect the harbour blockade to this local road interdiction.
A surviving flood survey locates an alternate ford accessible only after the working stops.
history: Successive road crews built the causeway to keep frontier traffic above seasonal floods. A Void Ascendant campaign now seeks to isolate those settlements by sea and land. Its operators use existing Shadow-tainted material in a bounded exterior siege construction. This collection introduces no change to Malachar’s sealed condition, reach or canonical history.
traversal: Establish convoy shelters, cross damaged spans on anchored lines and unload the working’s basalt weights in a sequence learned from visible tension. The finale concerns the bridge and the convoy. Pursuing the fleeing enemy beyond the exterior route is unavailable; there is no reward for approaching the canonical seal.

story.role: Records from the bells, survey and harbour campaign reveal a local bridge interdiction. Sabine and Jolant use that knowledge to protect a frontier convoy, ending at the exterior road with Malachar’s prison untouched.
